tools.name: bb_search
tools.description: Unified indexed retrieval for symbol lists, content, exact symbol source, or files. This is retrieval, not natural-language explanation or code analysis.

query.description: symbol/content query; also accepted as the exact symbol name

symbolName.description: exact symbol name for symbol mode

language.description: filter by language (e.g. typescript, python, go)

symbolKind.description: filter by symbol kind (function, class, variable, interface, enum, ...)

includeContent.description: include a code snippet per result (default false)

regex.description: treat query as a regex against symbol names (default false)

documentation.summary: Unified lexical, content, exact-symbol, and file retrieval.

returns: Indexed matches with file and line provenance
Exact symbol or bounded file source in retrieval modes
errors: Missing mode-specific query, symbolName, or filePath
limitations: Results reflect the current index and may be stale
Content search is lexical; use bb_ask for semantic discovery
tools.performance: Pagination and result limits bound retrieval; exact indexed lookup is preferred over content scanning.
tools.safety: Read-only. It does not refresh the index or modify source files.
tools.evidence: Paths, line ranges, symbol kinds, and source snippets are indexed evidence; stale flags qualify that evidence.

tools.name: bb_ask
tools.description: Answer a question about the codebase using semantic search over the index. Returns matched symbols with similarity scores.
limitations: Semantic similarity discovers candidates but does not independently prove a claim
Local word vectors provide lexical-quality fallback rather than model-quality semantics
tools.performance: The limit bounds returned semantic matches; embedding coverage and model choice affect ranking quality.
tools.safety: Read-only. It does not write source or silently rebuild embeddings.
tools.evidence: Treat matched symbols and resolvable source locations as evidence; treat generated explanation as interpretation.

tools.name: bb_health
tools.description: Unified index health: file/symbol/relationship/imports counts, embedding model + coverage, schema version, runtime, and file freshness. Use verbose=true for per-language breakdown and stale-file names, refresh=true to reindex before reporting, integrity=true for the 12-point index health check, complete=true for full (not sampled) freshness, includeAnalysisRuns=true for persisted run/finding totals, history=true for persisted analysis history.

force.description: force a full in-place reindex before reporting

wait.description: wait for refresh to finish (default true)

documentation.summary: Unified index, schema, freshness, embeddings, runtime, integrity, and analysis history.

returns: Index, schema, runtime, freshness, and embedding health
limitations: Sampled freshness is not a complete filesystem proof
Embedding coverage reports stored state, not semantic quality
tools.performance: Sampled freshness is the default; complete freshness and integrity checks intentionally cost more.
tools.safety: Status is read-only. refresh=true explicitly mutates only index data; force=true performs a full in-place reindex.
tools.evidence: Counts and versions come from the brain database; freshness compares indexed metadata with the filesystem.

tools.name: bb_patterns
tools.description: Detect orphaned code, framework patterns, anti-patterns, and architecture issues. Use scope=orphaned for dead code; scope=all (default) for the full pattern scan with the optional pattern/confidence filters.

scope.description: orphaned only, or all pattern classes (default all)

includeOrphaned.description: include orphaned-code patterns in an all scan (default true)

recordRun.description: persist this scan as an analysis run

documentation.summary: Pattern/orphan analysis with optional persisted run history.

returns: Pattern findings with confidence and locations
limitations: Orphan status is static incoming-reference evidence, not proof that code is unused
Framework and anti-pattern detection is heuristic and confidence-qualified
tools.performance: The result limit and confidence threshold bound reporting; history access is separately limited.
tools.safety: Source is read-only. recordRun writes only analysis-history records in the brain database.
tools.evidence: Every finding is confidence-qualified and tied to indexed files, symbols, or relationships.

tools.name: bb_security
tools.description: Cross-language security scan: SQL injection, XSS, command injection, hardcoded secrets, weak crypto.

recordRun.description: persist this scan as an analysis run

documentation.summary: Cross-language findings with optional persisted run history.

limitations: Static taint analysis can produce false positives and false negatives
It is not runtime testing or a penetration test
tools.performance: Indexed flow analysis and output/history limits bound work and response size.
tools.safety: Source is read-only. recordRun writes only analysis-history records in the brain database.
tools.evidence: A finding is supported by indexed source/sink locations and relationship paths; severity does not imply exploitability.

tools.name: bb_visualize
tools.description: Scoped dependency and architecture visualization over the canonical graph engine, with explicit filters, provenance, truncation, machine-readable JSON, and self-contained HTML.

target.description: file, module, symbol, or feature target

documentation.summary: Scoped canonical dependency graphs with explicit truncation and provenance.

returns: Text, JSON, or self-contained HTML projection
errors: Missing target for a scoped graph
limitations: The graph reflects static indexed relationships
Nodes and links beyond configured budgets are omitted and reported
tools.performance: maxNodes, maxLinks, scope, relationshipTypes, and languages constrain graph construction.
tools.safety: Read-only. HTML output contains the same bounded graph as JSON and does not mutate the project.
tools.evidence: Nodes and links resolve to canonical indexed entities; links with omitted endpoints are not emitted.

tools.name: bb_migrate
tools.description: Read-only single or batch migration planning with dependency order, explicit effort methodology, library mappings, risks, truncation, and unsupported cases.

symbolNames.description: one or more symbols to migrate

documentation.summary: Batch cross-language migration plans with ordering, methodology, and unsupported mappings.

returns: Effort methodology, library mappings, and risks
limitations: Plans are estimates, not translated source
Library mappings are advisory and unsupported routes remain explicit
tools.performance: Requests are capped at 100 symbols and dependency traversal is bounded.
tools.safety: Read-only. It does not generate, replace, or compile target-language source.
tools.evidence: Dependency ordering comes from indexed relationships; effort and mappings are labeled methodology-driven estimates.

tools.name: bb_analyze
tools.description: Unified evidence-backed analysis over graph relationships, dependencies, statistics, complexity, impact, and test intelligence. Select exactly one mode.

documentation.summary: One typed analysis surface replacing standalone relationship and test intelligence names.

returns: Graph, dependency, complexity, impact, or test evidence
errors: Missing target for a target-based mode
Option irrelevant to the selected mode
limitations: Static relationships cannot establish runtime behavior
Test results describe indexed static evidence, not executed coverage
tools.performance: Mode-specific limits and graph traversal bounds prevent unbounded output.
tools.safety: Read-only. Analysis never creates tests or edits source.
tools.evidence: Findings derive from brain_* symbols, files, relationships, complexity, and test-file classifications.

tools.name: bb_doc
tools.description: Generate read-only, evidence-backed documentation with resolvable citations. Supports symbol, file, module, feature, API, project, and documentation-coverage modes in Markdown or JSON.

target.description: symbol, file, module, feature, or API target; optional for project and coverage

documentation.summary: Cited Markdown or JSON documentation over indexed source and relationships.

limitations: Unknown facts remain explicit rather than inferred without support
Stale evidence is qualified and cannot silently become current
tools.performance: Evidence count and maxTokens impose explicit response budgets.
tools.safety: Read-only. It never refreshes implicitly, writes source, or invokes bb_edit.
tools.evidence: Claims are classified as extracted, inferred, generated, or unknown and carry resolvable citations where applicable.

tools.name: bb_edit
tools.description: Unified, validated source mutation. Discriminated by mode: write, update, insert, delete, or refactor. Supports dry-run previews, separator/symlink-safe paths, AST byte bounds, caller protection, rollback on validation failure, formatting, and reindexing.

documentation.summary: Unified safe source editing with preview, validation, rollback, and reindex.

returns: Structured mutation result or dry-run preview
Validation, formatting, rollback, and reindex status
Affected paths and caller protection outcomes
errors: Stale or ambiguous indexed symbol bounds
Caller protection, parse, formatting, or reindex failure
limitations: Named symbol edits require a fresh index
Refactoring is identifier-aware static rewriting, not a full language-server proof
tools.performance: Only affected files are written, formatted, validated, and reindexed.
tools.safety: Write-capable. Uses project-root path checks, atomic writes, snapshots, validation, and rollback; use dryRun before risky edits.
tools.evidence: Mutation bounds come from indexed AST bytes; validation and reindex state report whether post-edit evidence is current.
